note: Every enabled entry below was verified live with `slt selftest`. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the field reference. Disabled entries document *why* they are off — that is deliberate: a surface that cannot answer honestly is worth recording, not deleting.

surfaces.name: Lyzem
surfaces.note: Third-party Telegram search engine. Disabled: the results page is byte-for-byte structurally identical for hits and misses (both titled 'Search results'), so there is no honest detection rule to write.

surfaces.name: TGStat
surfaces.note: Rich channel analytics, but returns HTTP 403 to datacenter IPs. Enable with --include-disabled behind a residential proxy.

surfaces.name: Telemetr
surfaces.note: Requires an account; unauthenticated requests 404 regardless of whether the channel exists.

surfaces.name: GitLab
surfaces.note: Uses the public users API, which returns an empty JSON array for an unknown handle — a clean signal instead of an HTML app shell.

surfaces.name: Keybase
surfaces.note: The highest-value pivot in this list: Keybase profiles cryptographically self-attest links to other platforms. Handles are capped at 16 characters, so longer Telegram handles cannot exist here.

surfaces.name: PyPI
surfaces.note: Detected by a positive marker on the profile page. PyPI serves a Cloudflare 'Client Challenge' (HTTP 200) for unknown users, so a status-code rule would read every miss as a hit.

surfaces.name: npm
surfaces.note: Uses the registry search API keyed on maintainer. The older /-/user/org.couchdb.user: endpoint now returns 401 to unauthenticated clients and cannot be used.

surfaces.name: Gravatar
surfaces.note: Returns a JSON profile that often carries a display name and verified account links.

surfaces.name: Steam
errorMsg: The specified profile could not be found

surfaces.name: Twitch
errorMsg: Sorry. Unless you've got a time machine
surfaces.note: Disabled: the mobile shell renders its not-found state in JavaScript, so the sentinel is present or absent depending on how much of the app shell ships. It reported a hit for an unregistered handle during selftest, which is the worst possible failure mode.

surfaces.name: VK
surfaces.note: High-value pivot: VK overlaps heavily with Telegram's Russian-speaking userbase. Unknown handles return a genuine 404, so the status-code rule holds even from datacenter IPs.

surfaces.name: Hacker News
surfaces.note: The rule is correct and works from a residential IP, but HN returns HTTP 429 ('Sorry.') to datacenter ranges. Disabled by default so it cannot silently produce inconclusive noise.

surfaces.name: Reddit
surfaces.note: Reddit serves an HTML block page (HTTP 403) to datacenter IPs for every handle. Disabled: it cannot distinguish hit from miss without residential egress or an API token.

surfaces.name: Medium
surfaces.note: Cloudflare returns HTTP 403 for every handle from datacenter IPs, hit or miss.

surfaces.name: YouTube
surfaces.note: Requests from the EU are redirected to consent.youtube.com before the channel renders, so neither the sentinel nor the profile markup is ever reached.
